<h1 id="grafana-http-api">Grafana HTTP API. v0.0.1</h1>

> Scroll down for code samples, example requests and responses. Select a language for code samples from the tabs above or the mobile navigation menu.

The Grafana backend exposes an HTTP API, the same API is used by the frontend to do
everything from saving dashboards, creating users and updating data sources.

Base URLs:

* <a href="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/api">https://raw.githubusercontent.com/api</a>

* <a href="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/api">https://raw.githubusercontent.com/api</a>

Email: <a href="mailto:hello@grafana.com">Grafana Labs</a> 
Web: <a href="https://grafana.com">Grafana Labs</a> 

# Authentication

* API Key (api_key)
    - Parameter Name: **Authorization**, in: header.

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: basic

<h1 id="grafana-http-api-datasources">datasources</h1>

If you are running Grafana Enterprise and have Fine-grained access control enabled, for some endpoints you would need to have relevant permissions. Refer to specific resources to understand what permissions are required.

## Get all data sources.

<a id="opIdgetDataSources"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://grafana.example.com/datasources \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /datasources`

If you are running Grafana Enterprise and have Fine-grained access control enabled
you need to have a permission with action: `datasources:read` and scope: `datasources:*`.

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "access": "string",
    "basicAuth": true,
    "database": "string",
    "id": 0,
    "isDefault": true,
    "jsonData": {},
    "name": "string",
    "orgId": 0,
    "readOnly": true,
    "type": "string",
    "typeLogoUrl": "string",
    "typeName": "string",
    "uid": "string",
    "url": "string",
    "user": "string"
  }
]
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": "string",
  "message": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": "string",
  "message": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "error": "string",
  "message": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="get-all-data-sources-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|(empty)|[DataSourceList](#schemadatasourcelist)|
|401|Unauthorized|UnauthorizedError is returned when the request is not authenticated.|[ErrorResponseBody](#schemaerrorresponsebody)|
|403|Forbidden|ForbiddenError is returned if the user/token has insufficient permissions to access the requested resource.|[ErrorResponseBody](#schemaerrorresponsebody)|
|500|Internal Server Error|InternalServerError is a general error indicating something went wrong internally.|[ErrorResponseBody](#schemaerrorresponsebody)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basic, api_key
</aside>

## Create a data source.

<a id="opIdaddDataSource"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://grafana.example.com/datasources \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "access": "string",
    "basicAuth": true,
    "basicAuthUser": "string",
    "database": "string",
    "isDefault": true,
    "jsonData": {},
    "name": "string",
    "secureJsonData": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    },
    "type": "string",
    "uid": "string",
    "url": "string",
    "user": "string",
    "withCredentials": true
  }'
```

`POST /datasources`

By defining `password` and `basicAuthPassword` under secureJsonData property
Grafana encrypts them securely as an encrypted blob in the database.
The response then lists the encrypted fields under secureJsonFields.

If you are running Grafana Enterprise and have Fine-grained access control enabled
you need to have a permission with action: `datasources:create`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "access": "string",
  "basicAuth": true,
  "basicAuthUser": "string",
  "database": "string",
  "isDefault": true,
  "jsonData": {},
  "name": "string",
  "secureJsonData": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "type": "string",
  "uid": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "user": "string",
  "withCredentials": true
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-data-source-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[AddDataSourceCommand](#schemaadddatasourcecommand)|true|none|
|» access|body|[DsAccess](#schemadsaccess)|false|none|
|» basicAuth|body|boolean|false|none|
|» basicAuthUser|body|string|false|none|
|» database|body|string|false|none|
|» isDefault|body|boolean|false|none|
|» jsonData|body|[Json](#schemajson)|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|none|
|» secureJsonData|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» type|body|string|false|none|
|» uid|body|string|false|none|
|» url|body|string|false|none|
|» user|body|string|false|none|
|» withCredentials|body|boolean|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "datasource": {
    "access": "string",
    "accessControl": {
      "property1": true,
      "property2": true
    },
    "basicAuth": true,
    "basicAuthUser": "string",
    "database": "string",
    "id": 0,
    "isDefault": true,
    "jsonData": {},
    "name": "string",
    "orgId": 0,
    "readOnly": true,
    "secureJsonFields": {
      "property1": true,
      "property2": true
    },
    "type": "string",
    "typeLogoUrl": "string",
    "uid": "string",
    "url": "string",
    "user": "string",
    "version": 0,
    "withCredentials": true
  },
  "id": 65,
  "message": "Data source added",
  "name": "My Data source"
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": "string",
  "message": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": "string",
  "message": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 409 Response

```json
{
  "error": "string",
  "message": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "error": "string",
  "message": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-data-source-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|(empty)|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|UnauthorizedError is returned when the request is not authenticated.|[ErrorResponseBody](#schemaerrorresponsebody)|
|403|Forbidden|ForbiddenError is returned if the user/token has insufficient permissions to access the requested resource.|[ErrorResponseBody](#schemaerrorresponsebody)|
|409|Conflict|ConflictError|[ErrorResponseBody](#schemaerrorresponsebody)|
|500|Internal Server Error|InternalServerError is a general error indicating something went wrong internally.|[ErrorResponseBody](#schemaerrorresponsebody)|

<h3 id="create-a-data-source-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|datasource|[DataSource](#schemadatasource)|true|none|none|
|id|integer(int64)|true|none|ID Identifier of the new data source.|
|message|string|true|none|Message Message of the deleted dashboard.|
|name|string|true|none|Name of the new data source.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basic, api_key
</aside>

## Gets all correlations.

<a id="opIdgetCorrelations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://grafana.example.com/datasources/correlations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /datasources/correlations`

<h3 id="gets-all-correlations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|Limit the maximum number of correlations to return per page|
|page|query|integer(int64)|false|Page index for starting fetching correlations|
|sourceUID|query|[string]|false|Source datasource UID filter to be applied to correlations|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
    "targetUID": "PE1C5CBDA0504A6A3",
    "type": "string",
    "uid": "50xhMlg9k"
  }
]
```

## Update an existing data source.

<a id="opIdupdateDataSourceByUID"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://grafana.example.com/datasources/uid/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "access": "string",
    "basicAuth": true,
    "basicAuthUser": "string",
    "database": "string",
    "isDefault": true,
    "jsonData": {},
    "name": "string",
    "secureJsonData": {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    },
    "type": "string",
    "uid": "string",
    "url": "string",
    "user": "string",
    "version": 0,
    "withCredentials": true
  }'
```

`PUT /datasources/uid/{uid}`

Similar to creating a data source, `password` and `basicAuthPassword` should be defined under
secureJsonData in order to be stored securely as an encrypted blob in the database. Then, the
encrypted fields are listed under secureJsonFields section in the response.

If you are running Grafana Enterprise and have Fine-grained access control enabled
you need to have a permission with action: `datasources:write` and scopes: `datasources:*`, `datasources:uid:*` and `datasources:uid:1` (single data source).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "access": "string",
  "basicAuth": true,
  "basicAuthUser": "string",
  "database": "string",
  "isDefault": true,
  "jsonData": {},
  "name": "string",
  "secureJsonData": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "type": "string",
  "uid": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "user": "string",
  "version": 0,
  "withCredentials": true
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-existing-data-source-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|uid|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[UpdateDataSourceCommand](#schemaupdatedatasourcecommand)|true|none|
|» access|body|[DsAccess](#schemadsaccess)|false|none|
|» basicAuth|body|boolean|false|none|
|» basicAuthUser|body|string|false|none|
|» database|body|string|false|none|
|» isDefault|body|boolean|false|none|

|» type|body|string|false|none|
|» uid|body|string|false|none|
|» url|body|string|false|none|
|» user|body|string|false|none|
|» version|body|integer(int64)|false|The previous version -- used for optimistic locking|
|» withCredentials|body|boolean|false|none|

## DataSource query metrics with expressions.

<a id="opIdqueryMetricsWithExpressions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://grafana.example.com/ds/query \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "debug": true,
    "from": "now-1h",
    "queries": [
      {
        "datasource": {
          "uid": "PD8C576611E62080A"
        },
        "format": "table",
        "intervalMs": 86400000,
        "maxDataPoints": 1092,
        "rawSql": "SELECT 1 as valueOne, 2 as valueTwo",
        "refId": "A"
      }
    ],
    "to": "now"
  }'
```

`POST /ds/query`

If you are running Grafana Enterprise and have Fine-grained access control enabled
you need to have a permission with action: `datasources:query`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "debug": true,
  "from": "now-1h",
  "queries": [
    {
      "datasource": {
        "uid": "PD8C576611E62080A"
      },
      "format": "table",
      "intervalMs": 86400000,
      "maxDataPoints": 1092,
      "rawSql": "SELECT 1 as valueOne, 2 as valueTwo",
      "refId": "A"
    }
  ],
  "to": "now"
}
```

<h3 id="datasource-query-metrics-with-expressions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[MetricRequest](#schemametricrequest)|true|none|
|» debug|body|boolean|false|none|
|» from|body|string|true|From Start time in epoch timestamps in milliseconds or relative using Grafana time units.|
|» queries|body|[[Json](#schemajson)]|true|queries.refId – Specifies an identifier of the query. Is optional and default to “A”.<br>queries.datasourceId – Specifies the data source to be queried. Each query in the request must have an unique datasourceId.<br>queries.maxDataPoints - Species maximum amount of data points that dashboard panel can render. Is optional and default to 100.<br>queries.intervalMs - Specifies the time interval in milliseconds of time series. Is optional and defaults to 1000.|
|» to|body|string|true|To End time in epoch timestamps in milliseconds or relative using Grafana time units.|

<h1 id="grafana-http-api-folders">folders</h1>

Folders are identified by the identifier (id) and the unique identifier (uid).
The identifier (id) of a folder is an auto-incrementing numeric value and is only unique per Grafana install.
The unique identifier (uid) of a folder can be used for uniquely identify folders between multiple Grafana installs. It’s automatically generated if not provided when creating a folder. The uid allows having consistent URLs for accessing folders and when syncing folders between multiple Grafana installs. This means that changing the title of a folder will not break any bookmarked links to that folder.
The uid can have a maximum length of 40 characters.

## Get all folders.

<a id="opIdgetFolders"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://grafana.example.com/folders \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /folders`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

It returns all folders that the authenticated user has permission to view.
If nested folders are enabled, it expects an additional query parameter with the parent folder UID
and returns the immediate subfolders that the authenticated user has permission to view.
If the parameter is not supplied then it returns immediate subfolders under the root
that the authenticated user has permission to view.

Use: /apis/folder.grafana.app/v1/namespaces/{ns}/folders

<h3 id="get-all-folders-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|Limit the maximum number of folders to return|
|page|query|integer(int64)|false|Page index for starting fetching folders|
|parentUid|query|string|false|The parent folder UID|
|permission|query|string|false|Set to `Edit` to return folders that the user can edit|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|permission|Edit|
|permission|View|

<h1 id="grafana-http-api-admin">admin</h1>

The Admin HTTP API does not currently work with an API Token. API Tokens are currently only linked to an organization and an organization role. They cannot be given the permission of server admin, only users can be given that permission. So in order to use these API calls you will have to use Basic Auth and the Grafana user must have the Grafana Admin permission. (The default admin user is called admin and has permission to use this API.)

## Fetch settings.

<a id="opIdadminGetSettings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://grafana.example.com/admin/settings \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /admin/settings`

If you are running Grafana Enterprise and have Fine-grained access control enabled, you need to have a permission with action `settings:read` and scopes: `settings:*`, `settings:auth.saml:` and `settings:auth.saml:enabled` (property level).

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "property1": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "property2": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  }
}
```

```json
{
  "error": "string",
  "message": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": "string",
  "message": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

<h1 id="grafana-http-api-annotations">annotations</h1>

Grafana Annotations feature released in Grafana 4.6. Annotations are saved in the Grafana database (sqlite, mysql or postgres). Annotations can be organization annotations that can be shown on any dashboard by configuring an annotation data source - they are filtered by tags. Or they can be tied to a panel on a dashboard and are then only shown on that panel.

## Find Annotations.

<a id="opIdgetAnnotations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://grafana.example.com/annotations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /annotations`

Starting in Grafana v6.4 regions annotations are now returned in one entity that now includes the timeEnd property.

<h3 id="find-annotations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|from|query|integer(int64)|false|Find annotations created after specific epoch datetime in milliseconds.|
|to|query|integer(int64)|false|Find annotations created before specific epoch datetime in milliseconds.|
|userId|query|integer(int64)|false|Limit response to annotations created by specific user.|
|userUID|query|string|false|Limit response to annotations created by a specific user, identified by UID.|
|alertId|query|integer(int64)|false|Find annotations for a specified alert rule by its ID.<br>deprecated: AlertID is deprecated and will be removed in future versions. Please use AlertUID instead.|
|alertUID|query|string|false|Find annotations for a specified alert rule by its UID.|
|dashboardId|query|integer(int64)|false|Find annotations that are scoped to a specific dashboard|
|dashboardUID|query|string|false|Find annotations that are scoped to a specific dashboard|
|panelId|query|integer(int64)|false|Find annotations that are scoped to a specific panel|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|Max limit for results returned.|
|tags|query|[string]|false|Use this to filter organization annotations. Organization annotations are annotations from an annotation data source that are not connected specifically to a dashboard or panel. You can filter by multiple tags.|
|type|query|string|false|Return alerts or user created annotations<br>Description:<br>- `alert`<br>- `annotation`|
|matchAny|query|boolean|false|Match any or all tags|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|type|alert|
|type|annotation|

## Create Annotation.

<a id="opIdpostAnnotation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://grafana.example.com/annotations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "dashboardId": 0,
    "dashboardUID": "string",
    "data": {},
    "panelId": 0,
    "tags": [
      "string"
    ],
    "text": "string",
    "time": 0,
    "timeEnd": 0
  }'
```

`POST /annotations`

Creates an annotation in the Grafana database. The dashboardId and panelId fields are optional. If they are not specified then an organization annotation is created and can be queried in any dashboard that adds the Grafana annotations data source. When creating a region annotation include the timeEnd property.
The format for `time` and `timeEnd` should be epoch numbers in millisecond resolution.
The response for this HTTP request is slightly different in versions prior to v6.4. In prior versions you would also get an endId if you where creating a region. But in 6.4 regions are represented using a single event with time and timeEnd properties.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "dashboardId": 0,
  "dashboardUID": "string",
  "data": {},
  "panelId": 0,
  "tags": [
    "string"
  ],
  "text": "string",
  "time": 0,
  "timeEnd": 0
}
```

<h3 id="create-annotation-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[PostAnnotationsCmd](#schemapostannotationscmd)|true|none|
|» dashboardId|body|integer(int64)|false|none|
|» dashboardUID|body|string|false|none|
|» data|body|[Json](#schemajson)|false|none|
|» panelId|body|integer(int64)|false|none|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|none|
|» text|body|string|true|none|
|» time|body|integer(int64)|false|none|
|» timeEnd|body|integer(int64)|false|none|

> Example responses

```json
  "id": 65,
  "message": "string"
}
```

```json
}
```

```json
}
```

```json
}
```

## Create Annotation in Graphite format.

<a id="opIdpostGraphiteAnnotation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://grafana.example.com/annotations/graphite \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "data": "string",
    "tags": null,
    "what": "string",
    "when": 0
  }'
```

`POST /annotations/graphite`

Creates an annotation by using Graphite-compatible event format. The `when` and `data` fields are optional. If `when` is not specified then the current time will be used as annotation’s timestamp. The `tags` field can also be in prior to Graphite `0.10.0` format (string with multiple tags being separated by a space).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": "string",
  "tags": null,
  "what": "string",
  "when": 0
}
```

<h1 id="grafana-http-api-libraryelements">library_elements</h1>

The identifier (ID) of a library element is an auto-incrementing numeric value that is unique per Grafana install.
The unique identifier (UID) of a library element uniquely identifies library elements between multiple Grafana installs. It’s automatically generated unless you specify it during library element creation. The UID provides consistent URLs for accessing library elements and when syncing library elements between multiple Grafana installs.
The maximum length of a UID is 40 characters.

## Get all library elements.

<a id="opIdgetLibraryElements"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://grafana.example.com/library-elements \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /library-elements`

Returns a list of all library elements the authenticated user has permission to view.
Use the `perPage` query parameter to control the maximum number of library elements returned; the default limit is `100`.
You can also use the `page` query parameter to fetch library elements from any page other than the first one.

<h3 id="get-all-library-elements-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|searchString|query|string|false|Part of the name or description searched for.|
|kind|query|integer(int64)|false|Kind of element to search for.<br>Description:<br>- 1 - library panels|
|sortDirection|query|string|false|Sort order of elements.<br>Description:<br>- alpha-asc: ascending<br>- alpha-desc: descending|
|typeFilter|query|string|false|A comma separated list of types to filter the elements by|
|excludeUid|query|string|false|Element UID to exclude from search results.|
|folderFilter|query|string|false|A comma separated list of folder ID(s) to filter the elements by.<br>Deprecated: Use FolderFilterUIDs instead.|
|folderFilterUIDs|query|string|false|A comma separated list of folder UID(s) to filter the elements by.|
|perPage|query|integer(int64)|false|The number of results per page.|
|page|query|integer(int64)|false|The page for a set of records, given that only perPage records are returned at a time. Numbering starts at 1.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|kind|1|
|sortDirection|alpha-asc|
|sortDirection|alpha-desc|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "result": {
    "elements": [
      {
        "description": "string",
        "folderId": 0,
        "folderUid": "string",
        "id": 0,
        "kind": 0,
        "meta": {
          "connectedDashboards": 0,
          "created": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
          "createdBy": {
            "avatarUrl": "string",
            "id": 0,
            "name": "string"
          },
          "folderName": "string",
          "folderUid": "string",
          "updated": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
          "updatedBy": {
            "avatarUrl": "string",
            "id": 0,
            "name": "string"
          }
        },
        "model": null,
        "name": "string",
        "orgId": 0,
        "schemaVersion": 0,
        "type": "string",
        "uid": "string",
        "version": 0
      }
    ],
    "page": 0,
    "perPage": 0,
    "totalCount": 0
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": "string",
  "message": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "error": "string",
  "message": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

<h1 id="grafana-http-api-queryhistory">query_history</h1>

The identifier (ID) of a query in query history is an auto-incrementing numeric value that is unique per Grafana install.
The unique identifier (UID) of a query history uniquely identifies queries in query history between multiple Grafana installs. It’s automatically generated. The UID provides consistent URLs for accessing queries in query history.

## Query history search.

<a id="opIdsearchQueries"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://grafana.example.com/query-history \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /query-history`

Returns a list of queries in the query history that matches the search criteria.
Query history search supports pagination. Use the `limit` parameter to control the maximum number of queries returned; the default limit is 100.
You can also use the `page` query parameter to fetch queries from any page other than the first one.

<h3 id="query-history-search-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|datasourceUid|query|[string]|false|List of data source UIDs to search for|
|searchString|query|string|false|Text inside query or comments that is searched for|
|onlyStarred|query|boolean|false|Flag indicating if only starred queries should be returned|
|sort|query|string|false|Sort method|
|page|query|integer(int64)|false|Use this parameter to access hits beyond limit. Numbering starts at 1. limit param acts as page size.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|Limit the number of returned results|
|from|query|integer(int64)|false|From range for the query history search|
|to|query|integer(int64)|false|To range for the query history search|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort|time-desc|
|sort|time-asc|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "result": {
    "page": 0,
    "perPage": 0,
    "queryHistory": [
      {
        "comment": "string",
        "createdAt": 0,
        "createdBy": 0,
        "datasourceUid": "string",
        "queries": {},
        "starred": true,
        "uid": "string"
      }
    ],
    "totalCount": 0
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": "string",
  "message": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "error": "string",
  "message": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="query-history-search-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|(empty)|[QueryHistorySearchResponse](#schemaqueryhistorysearchresponse)|
|401|Unauthorized|UnauthorizedError is returned when the request is not authenticated.|[ErrorResponseBody](#schemaerrorresponsebody)|
|500|Internal Server Error|InternalServerError is a general error indicating something went wrong internally.|[ErrorResponseBody](#schemaerrorresponsebody)|

<h1 id="grafana-http-api-orgs">orgs</h1>

The Admin Organizations HTTP API does not currently work with an API Token. API Tokens are currently only linked to an organization and an organization role. They cannot be given the permission of server admin, only users can be given that permission. So in order to use these API calls you will have to use Basic Auth and the Grafana user must have the Grafana Admin permission (The default admin user is called `admin` and has permission to use this API).

<h1 id="grafana-http-api-accesscontrol">access_control</h1>

The API can be used to create, update, get and list roles, and create or remove built-in role assignments. To use the API, you would need to enable fine-grained access control.
This only available in Grafana Enterprise.
The API does not currently work with an API Token. So in order to use these API endpoints you will have to use Basic auth.

## Get all roles.

<a id="opIdlistRoles"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://grafana.example.com/access-control/roles \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /access-control/roles`

Gets all existing roles. The response contains all global and organization local roles, for the organization which user is signed in.

You need to have a permission with action `roles:read` and scope `roles:*`.

The `delegatable` flag reduces the set of roles to only those for which the signed-in user has permissions to assign.

<h3 id="get-all-roles-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|delegatable|query|boolean|false|none|
|includeHidden|query|boolean|false|none|
|targetOrgId|query|integer(int64)|false|none|

## Create a new custom role.

<a id="opIdcreateRole"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://grafana.example.com/access-control/roles \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "string",
    "displayName": "string",
    "global": true,
    "group": "string",
    "hidden": true,
    "name": "string",
    "permissions": [
      {
        "action": "string",
        "created": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
        "scope": "string",
        "updated": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
      }
    ],
    "uid": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /access-control/roles`

Creates a new custom role and maps given permissions to that role. Note that roles with the same prefix as Fixed Roles can’t be created.

You need to have a permission with action `roles:write` and scope `permissions:type:delegate`. `permissions:type:delegate` scope ensures that users can only create custom roles with the same, or a subset of permissions which the user has.
For example, if a user does not have required permissions for creating users, they won’t be able to create a custom role which allows to do that. This is done to prevent escalation of privileges.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "string",
  "displayName": "string",
  "global": true,
  "group": "string",
  "hidden": true,
  "name": "string",
  "permissions": [
    {
      "action": "string",
      "created": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "scope": "string",
      "updated": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    }
  ],
  "uid": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-custom-role-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateRoleForm](#schemacreateroleform)|true|none|
|» description|body|string|false|none|
|» displayName|body|string|false|none|
|» global|body|boolean|false|none|
|» group|body|string|false|none|
|» hidden|body|boolean|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|none|
|» permissions|body|[[Permission](#schemapermission)]|false|none|
|» uid|body|string|false|none|

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
```

`DELETE /access-control/roles/{roleUID}`

Delete a role with the given UID, and it’s permissions. If the role is assigned to a built-in role, the deletion operation will fail, unless force query param is set to true, and in that case all assignments will also be deleted.

## Set user role assignments.

<a id="opIdsetUserRoles"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://grafana.example.com/access-control/users/0/roles \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "global": true,
    "includeHidden": true,
    "roleUids": [
      "string"
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /access-control/users/{userId}/roles`

Update the user’s role assignments to match the provided set of UIDs. This will remove any assigned roles that aren’t in the request and add roles that are in the set but are not already assigned to the user.
Roles mapped through group attribute sync are not impacted.
If you want to add or remove a single role, consider using Add a user role assignment or Remove a user role assignment instead.

You need to have a permission with action `users.roles:add` and `users.roles:remove` and scope `permissions:type:delegate` for each. The delegate scope is required for permissions on roles being added.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "global": true,
  "includeHidden": true,
  "roleUids": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="set-user-role-assignments-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|userId|path|integer(int64)|true|none|
|targetOrgId|query|integer(int64)|false|none|
|body|body|[SetUserRolesCommand](#schemasetuserrolescommand)|true|none|
|» global|body|boolean|false|none|
|» includeHidden|body|boolean|false|none|
|» roleUids|body|[string]|false|none|

```json
}
```

## Add a user role assignment.

<a id="opIdaddUserRole"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://grafana.example.com/access-control/users/0/roles \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "global": true,
    "roleUid": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /access-control/users/{userId}/roles`

Assign a role to a specific user. For bulk updates consider Set user role assignments.

You need to have a permission with action `users.roles:add` and scope `permissions:type:delegate`. `permissions:type:delegate` scope ensures that users can only assign roles which have same, or a subset of permissions which the user has. For example, if a user does not have required permissions for creating users, they won’t be able to assign a role which will allow to do that. This is done to prevent escalation of privileges.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "global": true,
  "roleUid": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="add-a-user-role-assignment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|userId|path|integer(int64)|true|none|
|body|body|[AddUserRoleCommand](#schemaadduserrolecommand)|true|none|
|» global|body|boolean|false|none|
|» roleUid|body|string|false|none|

```json
  "message": "string"
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
  "status": "string"
}
```

## Set resource permissions.

<a id="opIdsetResourcePermissions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://grafana.example.com/access-control/string/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "permissions": [
      {
        "builtInRole": "string",
        "permission": "string",
        "teamId": 0,
        "userId": 0
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /access-control/{resource}/{resourceID}`

Assigns permissions for a resource by a given type (`:resource`) and `:resourceID` to one or many
assignment types. Allowed resources are `datasources`, `teams`, `dashboards`, `folders`, and `serviceaccounts`.
Refer to the `/access-control/{resource}/description` endpoint for allowed Permissions.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "permissions": [
    {
      "builtInRole": "string",
      "permission": "string",
      "teamId": 0,
      "userId": 0
    }
  ]
}
```

|» permissions|body|[[SetResourcePermissionCommand](#schemasetresourcepermissioncommand)]|false|none|

<h1 id="grafana-http-api-licensing">licensing</h1>

If you are running Grafana Enterprise and have Fine-grained access control enabled, for some endpoints you would need to have relevant permissions. Refer to specific resources to understand what permissions are required.

This API allows you to interact programmatically with the Reporting feature.
Reporting is only available in Grafana Enterprise. Read more about Grafana Enterprise.
If you have Fine-grained access Control enabled, for some endpoints you would need to have relevant permissions. Refer to specific resources to understand what permissions are required.

## List reports.

<a id="opIdgetReports"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://grafana.example.com/reports \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /reports`

Available to org admins only and with a valid or expired license.

You need to have a permission with action `reports:read` with scope `reports:*`.

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json

    "created": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
```

## Create a report.

<a id="opIdcreateReport"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://grafana.example.com/reports \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "dashboards": [
      {
        "dashboard": {
          "id": 0,
          "name": "string",
          "uid": "string"
        },
        "reportVariables": null,
        "timeRange": {
          "from": "string",
          "to": "string"
        }
      }
    ],
    "enableCsv": true,
    "enableDashboardUrl": true,
    "formats": [
      "string"
    ],
    "message": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "options": {
      "csvEncoding": "string",
      "layout": "string",
      "orientation": "string",
      "pdfCombineOneFile": true,
      "pdfShowTemplateVariables": true,
      "timeRange": {
        "from": "string",
        "to": "string"
      }
    },
    "recipients": "string",
    "replyTo": "string",
    "scaleFactor": 0,
    "schedule": {
      "dayOfMonth": "string",
      "endDate": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "frequency": "string",
      "intervalAmount": 0,
      "intervalFrequency": "string",
      "startDate": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "timeZone": "string",
      "workdaysOnly": true
    },
    "state": "string",
    "subject": "string",
    "urls": [
      {
        "title": "string",
        "url": "string"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /reports`

Available to org admins only and with a valid license.

You need to have a permission with action `reports.admin:create`.

## Send a report.

<a id="opIdsendReport"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://grafana.example.com/reports/email \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "emails": "string",
    "id": "string",
    "uid": "string",
    "useEmailsFromReport": true
  }'
```

`POST /reports/email`

Generate and send a report. This API waits for the report to be generated before returning. We recommend that you set the client’s timeout to at least 60 seconds. Available to org admins only and with a valid license.

Only available in Grafana Enterprise v7.0+.
This API endpoint is experimental and may be deprecated in a future release. On deprecation, a migration strategy will be provided and the endpoint will remain functional until the next major release of Grafana.

You need to have a permission with action `reports:send`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "emails": "string",
  "id": "string",
  "uid": "string",
  "useEmailsFromReport": true
}
```

<h3 id="send-a-report-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ReportEmail](#schemareportemail)|true|none|
|» emails|body|string|false|Comma-separated list of emails to which to send the report to.|
|» id|body|string(int64)|false|Numeric ID of the report. Can send either ID or UID. If both are present, UID takes precedence.|
|» uid|body|string|false|UID of the report. Can send either ID or UID. If both are present, UID takes precedence.|
|» useEmailsFromReport|body|boolean|false|Send the report to the emails specified in the report. Required if emails is not present.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": "string",
  "message": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": "string",
  "message": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": "string",
  "message": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "error": "string",
  "message": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "error": "string",
  "message": "string",
  "status": "string"
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|An OKResponse is returned if the request was successful.|[SuccessResponseBody](#schemasuccessresponsebody)|
|400|Bad Request|BadRequestError is returned when the request is invalid and it cannot be processed.|[ErrorResponseBody](#schemaerrorresponsebody)|
|401|Unauthorized|UnauthorizedError is returned when the request is not authenticated.|[ErrorResponseBody](#schemaerrorresponsebody)|
|403|Forbidden|ForbiddenError is returned if the user/token has insufficient permissions to access the requested resource.|[ErrorResponseBody](#schemaerrorresponsebody)|
|404|Not Found|NotFoundError is returned when the requested resource was not found.|[ErrorResponseBody](#schemaerrorresponsebody)|
|500|Internal Server Error|InternalServerError is a general error indicating something went wrong internally.|[ErrorResponseBody](#schemaerrorresponsebody)|

<h1 id="grafana-http-api-serviceaccounts">service_accounts</h1>

If you are running Grafana Enterprise, for some endpoints you'll need to have specific permissions. Refer to [Role-based access control permissions](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/administration/roles-and-permissions/access-control/custom-role-actions-scopes/) for more information.

## Create service account

<a id="opIdcreateServiceAccount"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://grafana.example.com/serviceaccounts \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "isDisabled": false,
    "name": "grafana",
    "role": "Admin"
  }'
```

`POST /serviceaccounts`

Required permissions (See note in the [introduction](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/developers/http_api/serviceaccount/#service-account-api) for an explanation):
action: `serviceaccounts:write` scope: `serviceaccounts:*`

Requires basic authentication and that the authenticated user is a Grafana Admin.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "isDisabled": false,
  "name": "grafana",
  "role": "Admin"
}
```

## Reload dashboard provisioning configurations.

<a id="opIdadminProvisioningReloadDashboards"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://grafana.example.com/admin/provisioning/dashboards/reload \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`POST /admin/provisioning/dashboards/reload`

Reloads the provisioning config files for dashboards again. It won’t return until the new provisioned entities are already stored in the database. In case of dashboards, it will stop polling for changes in dashboard files and then restart it with new configurations after returning.
If you are running Grafana Enterprise and have Fine-grained access control enabled, you need to have a permission with action `provisioning:reload` and scope `provisioners:dashboards`.

## Create new user.

<a id="opIdadminCreateUser"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://grafana.example.com/admin/users \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "email": "string",
    "login": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "orgId": 0,
    "password": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /admin/users`

If you are running Grafana Enterprise and have Fine-grained access control enabled, you need to have a permission with action `users:create`.
Note that OrgId is an optional parameter that can be used to assign a new user to a different organization when `auto_assign_org` is set to `true`.

> Body parameter

```json

  "email": "string",
  "login": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "orgId": 0,
  "password": "string"
}
```

## Revoke auth token for user.

<a id="opIdadminRevokeUserAuthToken"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://grafana.example.com/admin/users/0/revoke-auth-token \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "authTokenId": 0
  }'
```

`POST /admin/users/{user_id}/revoke-auth-token`

Revokes the given auth token (device) for the user. User of issued auth token (device) will no longer be logged in and will be required to authenticate again upon next activity.
If you are running Grafana Enterprise and have Fine-grained access control enabled, you need to have a permission with action `users.authtoken:update` and scope `global.users:*`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "authTokenId": 0
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|user_id|path|integer(int64)|true|none|
|body|body|[RevokeAuthTokenCmd](#schemarevokeauthtokencmd)|true|none|

## Converts a Prometheus rule group into a Grafana rule group and creates or updates it within the specified namespace.

<a id="opIdRouteConvertPrometheusCortexPostRuleGroup"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://grafana.example.com/convert/api/prom/rules/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/yaml' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{"interval":0,"labels":{"property1":"string","property2":"string"},"limit":0,"name":"string","query_offset":"string","rules":[{"alert":"string","annotations":{"property1":"string","property2":"string"},"expr":"string","for":"string","keep_firing_for":"string","labels":{"property1":"string","property2":"string"},"record":"string"}]}'
```

`POST /convert/api/prom/rules/{NamespaceTitle}`

If the group already exists and was not imported from a Prometheus-compatible source initially,
it will not be replaced and an error will be returned.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "interval": 0,
  "labels": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "limit": 0,
  "name": "string",
  "query_offset": "string",
  "rules": [
    {
      "alert": "string",
      "annotations": {
        "property1": "string",
        "property2": "string"
      },
      "expr": "string",
      "for": "string",
      "keep_firing_for": "string",
      "labels": {
        "property1": "string",
        "property2": "string"
      },
      "record": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|

|x-grafana-alerting-datasource-uid|header|string|false|none|
|x-grafana-alerting-recording-rules-paused|header|boolean|false|none|
|x-grafana-alerting-alert-rules-paused|header|boolean|false|none|
|x-grafana-alerting-target-datasource-uid|header|string|false|none|

|body|body|[PrometheusRuleGroup](#schemaprometheusrulegroup)|false|none|
|» interval|body|[Duration](#schemaduration)|false|A Duration represents the elapsed time between two instants<br>as an int64 nanosecond count. The representation limits the<br>largest representable duration to approximately 290 years.|
|» labels|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» limit|body|integer(int64)|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|none|

## When creating a snapshot using the API, you have to provide the full dashboard payload including the snapshot data. This endpoint is designed for the Grafana UI.

<a id="opIdcreateDashboardSnapshot"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://grafana.example.com/snapshots \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "apiVersion": "string",
    "dashboard": {
      "Object": {
        "property1": null,
        "property2": null
      }
    },
    "deleteKey": "string",
    "expires": 0,
    "external": false,
    "key": "string",
    "kind": "string",
    "name": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /snapshots`

Snapshot public mode should be enabled or authentication is required.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "apiVersion": "string",
  "dashboard": {
    "Object": {
      "property1": null,
      "property2": null
    }
  },
  "deleteKey": "string",
  "expires": 0,
  "external": false,
  "key": "string",
  "kind": "string",
  "name": "string"
```

<h1 id="grafana-http-api-search">search</h1>

## search

<a id="opIdsearch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://grafana.example.com/search \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /search`

<h3 id="search-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|query|query|string|false|Search Query|
|tag|query|[string]|false|List of tags to search for|
|type|query|string|false|Type to search for, dash-folder or dash-db<br>Description:<br>- `dash-folder` - Search for folder<br>- `dash-db` - Seatch for dashboard|
|dashboardIds|query|[integer(int64)]|false|List of dashboard id’s to search for<br>This is deprecated: users should use the `dashboardUIDs` query parameter instead|
|dashboardUIDs|query|[string]|false|List of dashboard uid’s to search for|
|folderIds|query|[integer(int64)]|false|List of folder id’s to search in for dashboards<br>If it's `0` then it will query for the top level folders<br>This is deprecated: users should use the `folderUIDs` query parameter instead<br><br>Deprecated: use FolderUIDs instead|
|folderUIDs|query|[string]|false|List of folder UID’s to search in for dashboards<br>If it's an empty string then it will query for the top level folders|
|starred|query|boolean|false|Flag indicating if only starred Dashboards should be returned|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|Limit the number of returned results (max 5000)|
|page|query|integer(int64)|false|Use this parameter to access hits beyond limit. Numbering starts at 1. limit param acts as page size. Only available in Grafana v6.2+.|
|permission|query|string|false|Set to `Edit` to return dashboards/folders that the user can edit|
|sort|query|string|false|Sort method; for listing all the possible sort methods use the search sorting endpoint.|
|deleted|query|boolean|false|Flag indicating if only soft deleted Dashboards should be returned|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|type|dash-folder|
|type|dash-db|
|permission|Edit|
|permission|View|
|sort|alpha-asc|
|sort|alpha-desc|

|204|No Content|An OKResponse is returned if the request was successful.|[SuccessResponseBody](#schemasuccessresponsebody)|

## Remove SSO Settings

<a id="opIdremoveProviderSettings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://grafana.example.com/v1/sso-settings/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /v1/sso-settings/{key}`

Removes the SSO Settings for a provider.

You need to have a permission with action `settings:write` and scope `settings:auth.<provider>:*`.

## Patch SSO Settings

<a id="opIdpatchProviderSettings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://grafana.example.com/v1/sso-settings/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "settings": {
      "property1": null,
      "property2": null
    }
  }'
```

`PATCH /v1/sso-settings/{key}`

Partially updates the SSO Settings for a provider. Only provided fields are updated.

You need to have a permission with action `settings:write` and scope `settings:auth.<provider>:*`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "settings": {
    "property1": null,
    "property2": null
  }
}
```

|key|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» settings|body|object|false|none|

<h2 id="tocS_AlertRuleNotificationSettings">AlertRuleNotificationSettings</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaalertrulenotificationsettings"></a>
<a id="schema_AlertRuleNotificationSettings"></a>

<a id="tocsalertrulenotificationsettings"></a>

```json
{
  "active_time_intervals": [
    "maintenance"
  ],
  "group_by": [
    "alertname",
    "grafana_folder",
    "cluster"
  ],
  "group_interval": "5m",
  "group_wait": "30s",
  "mute_time_intervals": [
    "maintenance"
  ],
  "policy": "\"Alerting Team\"",
  "receiver": "grafana-default-email",
  "repeat_interval": "4h"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|active_time_intervals|[string]|false|none|Override the times when notifications should not be muted. These must match the name of a mute time interval defined<br>in the alertmanager configuration time_intervals section. All notifications will be suppressed unless they are sent<br>at the time that matches any interval.|
|group_by|[string]|false|none|Override the labels by which incoming alerts are grouped together. For example, multiple alerts coming in for<br>cluster=A and alertname=LatencyHigh would be batched into a single group. To aggregate by all possible labels<br>use the special value '...' as the sole label name.<br>This effectively disables aggregation entirely, passing through all alerts as-is. This is unlikely to be what<br>you want, unless you have a very low alert volume or your upstream notification system performs its own grouping.<br>Must include 'alertname' and 'grafana_folder' if not using '...'.|
|group_interval|string|false|none|Override how long to wait before sending a notification about new alerts that are added to a group of alerts for<br>which an initial notification has already been sent. (Usually ~5m or more.)|
|group_wait|string|false|none|Override how long to initially wait to send a notification for a group of alerts. Allows to wait for an<br>inhibiting alert to arrive or collect more initial alerts for the same group. (Usually ~0s to few minutes.)|
|mute_time_intervals|[string]|false|none|Override the times when notifications should be muted. These must match the name of a mute time interval defined<br>in the alertmanager configuration time_intervals section. When muted it will not send any notifications, but<br>otherwise acts normally.|
|policy|string|false|none|Name of the notification policy to route alerts through.<br>Mutually exclusive with all other fields, cannot be used with contact point routing via the "receiver" field.|
|receiver|string|true|none|Name of the receiver to send notifications to.|
|repeat_interval|string|false|none|Override how long to wait before sending a notification again if it has already been sent successfully for an<br>alert. (Usually ~3h or more).<br>Note that this parameter is implicitly bound by Alertmanager's `--data.retention` configuration flag.<br>Notifications will be resent after either repeat_interval or the data retention period have passed, whichever<br>occurs first. `repeat_interval` should not be less than `group_interval`.|

When parsed as part of a pkix.Name structure in a crypto/x509 type,
the Value will be

- a string if the ASN.1 type is PrintableString, IA5String,
NumericString, BMPString, T61String, or UTF8String;
- an int64 if the ASN.1 type is INTEGER;
- an asn1.BitString if the ASN.1 type is BIT STRING;
- a []byte if the ASN.1 type is OCTET STRING;
- an asn1.ObjectIdentifier if the ASN.1 type is OBJECT IDENTIFIER;
- a time.Time if the ASN.1 type is UTCTIME or GENERALIZEDTIME;
- a bool if the ASN.1 type is BOOLEAN;
- nil if the ASN.1 type is NULL;
- an asn1.RawValue otherwise.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Type|[ObjectIdentifier](#schemaobjectidentifier)|false|none|none|
|Value|object|false|none|none|

Each Field is well typed by its FieldType and supports optional Labels.

A Frame is a general data container for Grafana. A Frame can be table data
or time series data depending on its content and field types.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Fields|[[Field](#schemafield)]|false|none|Fields are the columns of a frame.<br>All Fields must be of the same the length when marshalling the Frame for transmission.<br>There should be no `nil` entries in the Fields slice (making them pointers was a mistake).|
|Meta|[FrameMeta](#schemaframemeta)|false|none|https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/master/packages/grafana-data/src/types/data.ts#L11<br>NOTE -- in javascript this can accept any `[key: string]: any;` however<br>this interface only exposes the values we want to be exposed|
|Name|string|false|none|Name is used in some Grafana visualizations.|
|RefID|string|false|none|RefID is a property that can be set to match a Frame to its originating query.|

|updated|string(date-time)|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_Extension">Extension</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaextension"></a>
<a id="schema_Extension"></a>
<a id="tocSextension"></a>
<a id="tocsextension"></a>

```json
{
  "Critical": true,
  "Id": [
    0
  ],
  "Value": [
    0
  ]
}
```

Extension represents the ASN.1 structure of the same name. See RFC
5280, section 4.2.

|Value|[integer(uint8)]|false|none|none|


A Field is essentially a slice of various types with extra properties and methods.
See NewField() for supported types.

The slice data in the Field is a not exported, so methods on the Field are used to to manipulate its data.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|config|[FieldConfig](#schemafieldconfig)|false|none|none|
|labels|[FrameLabels](#schemaframelabels)|false|none|Labels are used to add metadata to an object.  The JSON will always be sorted keys|
|name|string|false|none|Name is default identifier of the field. The name does not have to be unique, but the combination<br>of name and Labels should be unique for proper behavior in all situations.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|color|object|false|none|Map values to a display color<br>NOTE: this interface is under development in the frontend... so simple map for now|
|custom|object|false|none|Panel Specific Values|
|decimals|integer(uint16)|false|none|none|
|description|string|false|none|Description is human readable field metadata|
|displayName|string|false|none|DisplayName overrides Grafana default naming, should not be used from a data source|
|displayNameFromDS|string|false|none|DisplayNameFromDS overrides Grafana default naming strategy.|
|filterable|boolean|false|none|Filterable indicates if the Field's data can be filtered by additional calls.|
|interval|number(double)|false|none|Interval indicates the expected regular step between values in the series.<br>When an interval exists, consumers can identify "missing" values when the expected value is not present.<br>The grafana timeseries visualization will render disconnected values when missing values are found it the time field.<br>The interval uses the same units as the values.  For time.Time, this is defined in milliseconds.|
|links|[[DataLink](#schemadatalink)]|false|none|The behavior when clicking on a result|
|mappings|[ValueMappings](#schemavaluemappings)|false|none|none|
|max|[ConfFloat64](#schemaconffloat64)|false|none|ConfFloat64 is a float64. It Marshals float64 values of NaN of Inf<br>to null.|
|min|[ConfFloat64](#schemaconffloat64)|false|none|ConfFloat64 is a float64. It Marshals float64 values of NaN of Inf<br>to null.|
|noValue|string|false|none|Alternative to empty string|
|path|string|false|none|Path is an explicit path to the field in the datasource. When the frame meta includes a path,<br>this will default to `${frame.meta.path}/${field.name}<br><br>When defined, this value can be used as an identifier within the datasource scope, and<br>may be used as an identifier to update values in a subsequent request|
|thresholds|[ThresholdsConfig](#schemathresholdsconfig)|false|none|ThresholdsConfig setup thresholds|
|type|[FieldTypeConfig](#schemafieldtypeconfig)|false|none|FieldTypeConfig has type specific configs, only one should be active at a time|
|unit|string|false|none|Numeric Options|
|writeable|boolean|false|none|Writeable indicates that the datasource knows how to update this value|

<h2 id="tocS_FloatHistogram">FloatHistogram</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemafloathistogram"></a>
<a id="schema_FloatHistogram"></a>
<a id="tocSfloathistogram"></a>
<a id="tocsfloathistogram"></a>

```json
{
  "Count": 0,
  "CounterResetHint": 0,
  "CustomValues": [
    0
  ],
  "PositiveBuckets": [
    0
  ],
  "PositiveSpans": [
    {
      "Length": 0,
      "Offset": 0
    }
  ],
  "Schema": 0,
  "Sum": 0,
  "ZeroCount": 0,
  "ZeroThreshold": 0
}
```

A FloatHistogram is needed by PromQL to handle operations that might result
in fractional counts. Since the counts in a histogram are unlikely to be too
large to be represented precisely by a float64, a FloatHistogram can also be
used to represent a histogram with integer counts and thus serves as a more
generalized representation.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Count|number(double)|false|none|Total number of observations. Must be zero or positive.|
|CounterResetHint|[CounterResetHint](#schemacounterresethint)|false|none|or alternatively that we are dealing with a gauge histogram, where counter resets do not apply.|
|CustomValues|[number(double)]|false|none|Holds the custom (usually upper) bounds for bucket definitions, otherwise nil.<br>This slice is interned, to be treated as immutable and copied by reference.<br>These numbers should be strictly increasing. This field is only used when the<br>schema is for custom buckets, and the ZeroThreshold, ZeroCount, NegativeSpans<br>and NegativeBuckets fields are not used in that case.|
|PositiveBuckets|[number(double)]|false|none|Observation counts in buckets. Each represents an absolute count and<br>must be zero or positive.|
|PositiveSpans|[[Span](#schemaspan)]|false|none|Spans for positive and negative buckets (see Span below).|
|Schema|integer(int32)|false|none|Currently valid schema numbers are -4 <= n <= 8 for exponential buckets.<br>They are all for base-2 bucket schemas, where 1 is a bucket boundary in<br>each case, and then each power of two is divided into 2^n logarithmic buckets.<br>Or in other words, each bucket boundary is the previous boundary times<br>2^(2^-n). Another valid schema number is -53 for custom buckets, defined by<br>the CustomValues field.|
|Sum|number(double)|false|none|Sum of observations. This is also used as the stale marker.|
|ZeroCount|number(double)|false|none|Observations falling into the zero bucket. Must be zero or positive.|
|ZeroThreshold|number(double)|false|none|Width of the zero bucket.|

Each Field is well typed by its FieldType and supports optional Labels.

A Frame is a general data container for Grafana. A Frame can be table data
or time series data depending on its content and field types.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Fields|[[Field](#schemafield)]|false|none|Fields are the columns of a frame.<br>All Fields must be of the same the length when marshalling the Frame for transmission.<br>There should be no `nil` entries in the Fields slice (making them pointers was a mistake).|
|Meta|[FrameMeta](#schemaframemeta)|false|none|https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/master/packages/grafana-data/src/types/data.ts#L11<br>NOTE -- in javascript this can accept any `[key: string]: any;` however<br>this interface only exposes the values we want to be exposed|
|Name|string|false|none|Name is used in some Grafana visualizations.|
|RefID|string|false|none|RefID is a property that can be set to match a Frame to its originating query.|

https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/master/packages/grafana-data/src/types/data.ts#L11
NOTE -- in javascript this can accept any `[key: string]: any;` however
this interface only exposes the values we want to be exposed

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|channel|string|false|none|Channel is the path to a stream in grafana live that has real-time updates for this data.|
|custom|object|false|none|Custom datasource specific values.|
|dataTopic|[DataTopic](#schemadatatopic)|false|none|none|
|executedQueryString|string|false|none|ExecutedQueryString is the raw query sent to the underlying system. All macros and templating<br>have been applied.  When metadata contains this value, it will be shown in the query inspector.|
|notices|[[Notice](#schemanotice)]|false|none|Notices provide additional information about the data in the Frame that<br>Grafana can display to the user in the user interface.|
|path|string|false|none|Path is a browsable path on the datasource.|
|pathSeparator|string|false|none|PathSeparator defines the separator pattern to decode a hierarchy. The default separator is '/'.|
|preferredVisualisationPluginId|string|false|none|PreferredVisualizationPluginId sets the panel plugin id to use to render the data when using Explore. If<br>the plugin cannot be found will fall back to PreferredVisualization.|
|preferredVisualisationType|[VisType](#schemavistype)|false|none|none|
|stats|[[QueryStat](#schemaquerystat)]|false|none|Stats is an array of query result statistics.|
|type|[FrameType](#schemaframetype)|false|none|A FrameType string, when present in a frame's metadata, asserts that the<br>frame's structure conforms to the FrameType's specification.<br>This property is currently optional, so FrameType may be FrameTypeUnknown even if the properties of<br>the Frame correspond to a defined FrameType.|
|typeVersion|[FrameTypeVersion](#schemaframetypeversion)|false|none|none|
|uniqueRowIdFields|[integer(int64)]|false|none|Array of field indices which values create a unique id for each row. Ideally this should be globally unique ID<br>but that isn't guarantied. Should help with keeping track and deduplicating rows in visualizations, especially<br>with streaming data with frequent updates.|

A FrameType string, when present in a frame's metadata, asserts that the
frame's structure conforms to the FrameType's specification.
This property is currently optional, so FrameType may be FrameTypeUnknown even if the properties of
the Frame correspond to a defined FrameType.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|global|[GlobalConfig](#schemaglobalconfig)|false|none|GlobalConfig defines configuration parameters that are valid globally<br>unless overwritten.|
|inhibit_rules|[[InhibitRule](#schemainhibitrule)]|false|none|none|
|muteTimeProvenances|object|false|none|none|
|mute_time_intervals|[[MuteTimeInterval](#schemamutetimeinterval)]|false|none|MuteTimeIntervals is deprecated and will be removed before Alertmanager 1.0.|
|receivers|[[GettableApiReceiver](#schemagettableapireceiver)]|false|none|Override with our superset receiver type|
|route|[Route](#schemaroute)|false|none|A Route is a node that contains definitions of how to handle alerts. This is modified<br>from the upstream alertmanager in that it adds the ObjectMatchers property.|
|templates|[string]|false|none|none|
|time_intervals|[[TimeInterval](#schematimeinterval)]|false|none|none|

```json
  },
```

```json
      "Type": 0,

      "Type": 0,
      "Value": "string"
    }
  ]
```


InhibitRule defines an inhibition rule that mutes alerts that match the
target labels if an alert matching the source labels exists.
Both alerts have to have a set of labels being equal.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|equal|[string]|false|none|A set of labels that must be equal between the source and target alert<br>for them to be a match.|
|source_match|object|false|none|SourceMatch defines a set of labels that have to equal the given<br>value for source alerts. Deprecated. Remove before v1.0 release.|
|source_match_re|[MatchRegexps](#schemamatchregexps)|false|none|none|
|source_matchers|[Matchers](#schemamatchers)|false|none|Matchers is a slice of Matchers that is sortable, implements Stringer, and<br>provides a Matches method to match a LabelSet against all Matchers in the<br>slice. Note that some users of Matchers might require it to be sorted.|
|target_match|object|false|none|TargetMatch defines a set of labels that have to equal the given<br>value for target alerts. Deprecated. Remove before v1.0 release.|
|target_match_re|[MatchRegexps](#schemamatchregexps)|false|none|none|
|target_matchers|[Matchers](#schemamatchers)|false|none|Matchers is a slice of Matchers that is sortable, implements Stringer, and<br>provides a Matches method to match a LabelSet against all Matchers in the<br>slice. Note that some users of Matchers might require it to be sorted.|

JSONWebKey represents a public or private key in JWK format. It can be
marshaled into JSON and unmarshaled from JSON.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Algorithm|string|false|none|Key algorithm, parsed from `alg` header.|
|CertificateThumbprintSHA1|[integer(uint8)]|false|none|X.509 certificate thumbprint (SHA-1), parsed from `x5t` header.|
|CertificateThumbprintSHA256|[integer(uint8)]|false|none|X.509 certificate thumbprint (SHA-256), parsed from `x5t#S256` header.|
|Certificates|[[Certificate](#schemacertificate)]|false|none|X.509 certificate chain, parsed from `x5c` header.|
|CertificatesURL|[URL](#schemaurl)|false|none|none|
|Key|object|false|none|Key is the Go in-memory representation of this key. It must have one<br>of these types:<br>- ed25519.PublicKey<br>- ed25519.PrivateKey<br>- *ecdsa.PublicKey<br>- *ecdsa.PrivateKey<br>- *rsa.PublicKey<br>- *rsa.PrivateKey<br>- []byte (a symmetric key)<br><br>When marshaling this JSONWebKey into JSON, the "kty" header parameter<br>will be automatically set based on the type of this field.|
|KeyID|string|false|none|Key identifier, parsed from `kid` header.|
|Use|string|false|none|Key use, parsed from `use` header.|

Name represents an X.509 distinguished name. This only includes the common
elements of a DN. Note that Name is only an approximation of the X.509
structure. If an accurate representation is needed, asn1.Unmarshal the raw
subject or issuer as an [RDNSequence].

|Locality|[string]|false|none|none|
|Names|[[AttributeTypeAndValue](#schemaattributetypeandvalue)]|false|none|Names contains all parsed attributes. When parsing distinguished names,<br>this can be used to extract non-standard attributes that are not parsed<br>by this package. When marshaling to RDNSequences, the Names field is<br>ignored, see ExtraNames.|

|TLSConfig|[TLSConfig](#schematlsconfig)|false|none|none|
|audience|string|false|none|Audience optionally specifies the intended audience of the<br>request.  If empty, the value of TokenURL is used as the<br>intended audience. Only used if<br>GrantType is set to "urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer".|

|client_secret|[Secret](#schemasecret)|false|none|none|
|client_secret_file|string|false|none|none|
|client_secret_ref|string|false|none|ClientSecretRef is the name of the secret within the secret manager to use as the client<br>secret.|
|endpoint_params|object|false|none|none|
|grant_type|string|false|none|GrantType is the OAuth2 grant type to use. It can be one of<br>"client_credentials" or "urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer" (RFC 7523).<br>Default value is "client_credentials"|
|iss|string|false|none|Iss is the OAuth client identifier used when communicating with<br>the configured OAuth provider. Default value is client_id. Only used if<br>GrantType is set to "urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer".|
|no_proxy|string|false|none|NoProxy contains addresses that should not use a proxy.|
|proxy_connect_header|[ProxyHeader](#schemaproxyheader)|false|none|none|
|proxy_from_environment|boolean|false|none|ProxyFromEnvironment makes use of net/http ProxyFromEnvironment function<br>to determine proxies.|
|proxy_url|[URL](#schemaurl)|false|none|none|
|scopes|[string]|false|none|none|
|signature_algorithm|string|false|none|SignatureAlgorithm is the RSA algorithm used to sign JWT token. Only used if<br>GrantType is set to "urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer".<br>Default value is RS256 and valid values RS256, RS384, RS512|
|token_url|string|false|none|none|

The embedded FieldConfig's display name must be set.
It corresponds to the QueryResultMetaStat on the frontend (https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/master/packages/grafana-data/src/types/data.ts#L53).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|color|object|false|none|Map values to a display color<br>NOTE: this interface is under development in the frontend... so simple map for now|
|custom|object|false|none|Panel Specific Values|
|decimals|integer(uint16)|false|none|none|
|description|string|false|none|Description is human readable field metadata|
|displayName|string|false|none|DisplayName overrides Grafana default naming, should not be used from a data source|
|displayNameFromDS|string|false|none|DisplayNameFromDS overrides Grafana default naming strategy.|
|filterable|boolean|false|none|Filterable indicates if the Field's data can be filtered by additional calls.|
|interval|number(double)|false|none|Interval indicates the expected regular step between values in the series.<br>When an interval exists, consumers can identify "missing" values when the expected value is not present.<br>The grafana timeseries visualization will render disconnected values when missing values are found it the time field.<br>The interval uses the same units as the values.  For time.Time, this is defined in milliseconds.|
|links|[[DataLink](#schemadatalink)]|false|none|The behavior when clicking on a result|
|mappings|[ValueMappings](#schemavaluemappings)|false|none|none|
|max|[ConfFloat64](#schemaconffloat64)|false|none|ConfFloat64 is a float64. It Marshals float64 values of NaN of Inf<br>to null.|
|min|[ConfFloat64](#schemaconffloat64)|false|none|ConfFloat64 is a float64. It Marshals float64 values of NaN of Inf<br>to null.|
|noValue|string|false|none|Alternative to empty string|
|path|string|false|none|Path is an explicit path to the field in the datasource. When the frame meta includes a path,<br>this will default to `${frame.meta.path}/${field.name}<br><br>When defined, this value can be used as an identifier within the datasource scope, and<br>may be used as an identifier to update values in a subsequent request|
|thresholds|[ThresholdsConfig](#schemathresholdsconfig)|false|none|ThresholdsConfig setup thresholds|
|type|[FieldTypeConfig](#schemafieldtypeconfig)|false|none|FieldTypeConfig has type specific configs, only one should be active at a time|
|unit|string|false|none|Numeric Options|
|value|number(double)|false|none|none|
|writeable|boolean|false|none|Writeable indicates that the datasource knows how to update this value|

<h2 id="tocS_Sample">Sample</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemasample"></a>
<a id="schema_Sample"></a>
<a id="tocSsample"></a>
<a id="tocssample"></a>

```json
{
  "DropName": true,
  "F": 0,
  "H": {
    "Count": 0,
    "CounterResetHint": 0,
    "CustomValues": [
      0
    ],
    "PositiveBuckets": [
      0
    ],
    "PositiveSpans": [
      {
        "Length": 0,
        "Offset": 0
      }
    ],
    "Schema": 0,
    "Sum": 0,
    "ZeroCount": 0,
    "ZeroThreshold": 0
  },
  "Metric": {},
  "T": 0
}
```

Sample is a single sample belonging to a metric. It represents either a float
sample or a histogram sample. If H is nil, it is a float sample. Otherwise,
it is a histogram sample.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|DropName|boolean|false|none|DropName is used to indicate whether the __name__ label should be dropped<br>as part of the query evaluation.|
|F|number(double)|false|none|none|
|H|[FloatHistogram](#schemafloathistogram)|false|none|A FloatHistogram is needed by PromQL to handle operations that might result<br>in fractional counts. Since the counts in a histogram are unlikely to be too<br>large to be represented precisely by a float64, a FloatHistogram can also be<br>used to represent a histogram with integer counts and thus serves as a more<br>generalized representation.|
|Metric|[Labels](#schemalabels)|false|none|Each name and value is preceded by its length, encoded as a single byte<br>for size 0-254, or the following 3 bytes little-endian, if the first byte is 255.<br>Maximum length allowed is 2^24 or 16MB.<br>Names are in order.|
|T|integer(int64)|false|none|none|

<a id="schemaupdatefoldercommand"></a>
<a id="schema_UpdateFolderCommand"></a>
<a id="tocSupdatefoldercommand"></a>
<a id="tocsupdatefoldercommand"></a>

```json
{
  "description": "string",
  "overwrite": true,
  "title": "string",
  "version": 0
}
```

UpdateFolderCommand captures the information required by the folder service
to update a folder. Use Move to update a folder's parent folder.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|description|string|false|none|NewDescription it's an optional parameter used for overriding the existing folder description|
|overwrite|boolean|false|none|Overwrite only used by the legacy folder implementation|
|title|string|false|none|NewTitle it's an optional parameter used for overriding the existing folder title|
|version|integer(int64)|false|none|Version only used by the legacy folder implementation|

<h2 id="tocS_Userinfo">Userinfo</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemauserinfo-1"></a>
<a id="schema_Userinfo"></a>
<a id="tocSuserinfo-1"></a>
<a id="tocsuserinfo-1"></a>

```json
{}
```

The Userinfo type is an immutable encapsulation of username and
password details for a [URL]. An existing Userinfo value is guaranteed
to have a username set (potentially empty, as allowed by RFC 2396),
and optionally a password.
